title: They increase peace (Berakhot 64a)
hook: the tractate ends: the wise increase peace in the world
tomorrow: you finished a whole book. how do you say goodbye to it?

segments.voice: What a week near the end of Berakhot. Each act, a blessing. All God does is for good. Water is our life. In all thy ways. Fill the gap. And yesterday: from strength to strength. Six lines, one page apart. Today the page runs out.
screen: `SIX LINES THIS WEEK.` → `FROM STRENGTH TO STRENGTH.` → `TODAY THE PAGE RUNS OUT.`

segments.voice: The last message in a group chat after a fight says a lot. A thumbs-up. A long paragraph. Silence. Endings tell you what something was for. Berakhot, the whole tractate of blessings, has to end somewhere. It started at night, with the Shema. It could have ended on a law or a warning. Instead its last lines are about people who learn, and its very last word is peace.
screen: `THE LAST MESSAGE SAYS A LOT.` → `ENDINGS SHOW THE POINT.` → `THE LAST WORD IS PEACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the ending, in plain words. Rabbi Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Hanina: those who learn Torah increase peace in the world. His proof is Isaiah: "And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children." Then a small, playful move. Don't read banayikh, your children, read bonayikh, your builders. Same Hebrew letters, a different word. The ones who learn are builders, and what they build is peace. Then the page strings psalms together, one after another. "Great peace have they that love Thy law; and there is no stumbling for them." Peace within your walls, for the sake of my brothers and friends. And the last one is from Psalm 29: "The LORD will give strength unto His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace." Look at that: strength, yesterday's word, then peace. Strength isn't the goal. It's what peace is built with. Something to tell a friend tonight: in Hebrew that final word, bashalom, with peace, closes the whole tractate of blessings.
screen: `THOSE WHO LEARN INCREASE PEACE.` · `NOT CHILDREN: BUILDERS.` · `STRENGTH, THEN PEACE.` · then, large: `THEY INCREASE PEACE.`

segments.voice: Think of someone you've bumped against lately, or drifted from. Write them one short text that builds instead of wins: a thank you, an I'm sorry, a how are you. Read it once slowly, and send it only if it feels right.
screen: `SOMEONE YOU BUMPED AGAINST.` · `ONE LINE THAT BUILDS.` · `SEND IT IF IT'S RIGHT.`

segments.voice: They increase peace. The last teaching in Berakhot: those who learn are builders, and they build peace.
Keep this one: they increase peace, builders, not winners. Forty-six of fifty, and a good week.
